baseline_text: **Which text of the law.** Act No. 595/2003 Coll. on income tax (zákon o dani z príjmov), version in force from 1 January 2026 to 30 December 2026. Act No. 261/2025 Coll. made the 2026 changes to §11 and §15; under §52zzzj(1) they apply first for the 2026 tax year. A further version in force from 31 December 2026 adds an exemption for informal carers (§9(1)(t)) and amends §11(4), but §52zzzm says those apply first for 2027. Penalties come from Act No. 563/2009 Coll., the Tax Procedure Code (daňový poriadok).

baseline_text: ## Who this applies to
closest_final_text: ## Who this applies to

baseline_text:
- **Residents.** A person with permanent residence (trvalý pobyt) or a home (bydlisko) in Slovakia, or who usually stays there, is taxed on worldwide income (§2(d)(1)). Staying at least 183 days in a calendar year, counting every started day, is usually staying. The tax year is the calendar year (§2(l)).
- **Non-residents.** They are taxed only on Slovak-source income (§2(e), §16). They get the spouse allowance and the child bonus only if Slovak income is at least 90% of their total income (§11(7), §33(9)). The detail is in sk-cross-border.
- **Employees** (§5). The employer withholds monthly advances. An employee with only §5 income from Slovak employers can ask an employer for the annual settlement (ročné zúčtovanie) by 15 February 2027 instead of filing (§38(1)). Otherwise they file DPFO type A.
- **Self-employed** (§6(1) and (2)): trades (živnosť), liberal professions, farmers and other independent activity. They file DPFO type B.
- **Rental income** (§6(3)), **capital income** (§7) and **other income** (§8), such as sale of property, securities or crypto-assets. These go on DPFO type B.
- **Who must file.** Anyone whose taxable income in 2026 exceeds 50% of the personal allowance, so EUR 2,983.37, or who has a tax loss (§32(1)). Income taxed finally by withholding is left out of that test.
- **Out of scope.** Companies, and the special tax on top state officials (§15a).

baseline_text: The bands and allowances are multiples of the subsistence minimum (životné minimum) in force on 1 January of the tax year (§11(2)(a)). For 2026 that is EUR 284.13 a month, set from 1 July 2025 by Measure No. 168/2025 Coll. Amounts below are that figure times the multiple, rounded to the cent (§47).

baseline_text: **How the bands work.** The law sets two separate bases (§4(1)). Base (a) is employment income after allowances, plus rental and other income. Base (b) is business income after allowances and losses. Each base is taxed on its own scale in §15(a): base (a) always on the 19% to 35% bands, base (b) at 15% if business revenue is EUR 100,000 or less, otherwise on the same bands.

Base (b) is business income after allowances and losses. Each base is taxed on its own scale in §15(a): base (a) always on the 19% to 35% bands, base (b) at 15% if business revenue is EUR 100,000 or less, otherwise on the same bands.

baseline_text: ## The taxable base
closest_final_text: ## The taxable base

baseline_text: **Employment (§5).** Gross pay including benefits in kind, minus the employee's compulsory social and health contributions (§5(8)). Pay for 2026 received by 31 January 2027 belongs to 2026 (§4(3)). Withholding and contributions are in [sk-payroll-social](sk-payroll-social.md).
closest_final_text: **Employment (§5).** Gross pay including benefits in kind, minus the employee's compulsory social and health contributions (§5(8)). Pay for 2026 received by 31 January 2027 belongs to 2026 (§4(3)). Withholding and contributions are in [sk-payroll-social](sk-payroll-social.md).

baseline_text:
**Self-employed (§6(1),(2)).** Revenue minus either:
- **actual expenses** (preukázateľné výdavky), with tax records or double-entry accounts (§6(11)); or
- **flat-rate expenses** of 60% of revenue, capped at EUR 20,000, if the person is not a VAT payer, or was one for only part of the year (§6(10)). The flat rate covers all expenses except the compulsory social and health contributions, which are deducted on top in the amount paid. The person still keeps a record of income and of inventory and receivables (§6(10), §6(11)(a),(d)).
closest_final_text:
**Self-employed (§6(1),(2)).** Revenue minus either:
- **actual expenses** (preukázateľné výdavky), with tax records or double-entry accounts (§6(11)); or
- **flat-rate expenses** of 60% of revenue, capped at EUR 20,000, if the person is not a VAT payer, or was one for only part of the year (§6(10)). The flat rate covers all expenses except the compulsory social and health contributions, which are deducted on top in the amount paid. The person still keeps a record of income and of inventory and receivables (§6(10), §6(11)(a),(d)).

baseline_text: The result is the business partial base. A tax loss can be carried forward five years. A micro-taxpayer (business revenue up to EUR 60,000, §2(w)) can use it in full; others only up to 50% of the business base (§30(1)).
closest_final_text: The result is the business partial base. A tax loss can be carried forward for the five immediately following tax periods. Full-base loss relief requires micro-taxpayer status **in the deduction period**, not just revenue up to EUR 60,000. Under §2(w), the individual's taxable §6(1),(2) revenue must not exceed EUR 60,000; exclude a dependent person who carries out a controlled transaction in that period, a person declared bankrupt, entering liquidation or granted a payment plan, and a period shorter than twelve consecutive months except one shortened by death. Others can deduct at most 50% of the business base (§30(1)). Thus a EUR 10,000 base and EUR 8,000 unexpired loss allow EUR 8,000 relief for a qualifying micro-taxpayer, but only EUR 5,000 for the same-revenue trader with a controlled transaction; EUR 3,000 remains subject to the original expiry date. Exactly EUR 60,000 passes the revenue condition; EUR 60,000.01 does not ([ITA §§2(w),30](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2003/595/20260101.html)).
disposition: F13 full microtaxpayer gates and5period expiry preserved

baseline_text: **The 15% rate.** It turns on business revenue under §6(1) and (2), not on profit. Revenue of EUR 100,000 or less gives 15% on the whole business base. Above EUR 100,000 the whole business base goes on the bands (§15(a)(2),(3)).
closest_final_text: **The 15% rate.** It turns on business revenue under §6(1) and (2), not on profit. Revenue of EUR 100,000 or less gives 15% on the whole business base. Above EUR 100,000 the whole business base goes on the bands (§15(a)(2),(3)).

baseline_text:
**Allowances (nezdaniteľné časti, §11).** They reduce only the employment and business bases, never rental, capital or other income (§11(1)).
- The personal allowance and the spouse allowance are tested on the tax base from §5 and §6(1),(2) income. A taxpayer who at the start of 2026 receives an old-age, early, service or similar foreign pension gets no personal allowance if the pension for the year, including the 13th pension, exceeds the allowance; otherwise the allowance is cut to the difference (§11(6)).
- The spouse allowance needs a spouse living with the taxpayer who cared for a minor child, received a care allowance, was a registered jobseeker, or is disabled (§11(4)). The spouse's own income is net of their contributions. Months count only if the conditions held at the start of the month (§11(5)).
- Allowances come off the employment base first, and only the rest comes off the business base (§11(12)).
closest_final_text:
**Allowances (nezdaniteľné časti, §11).** They reduce only the employment and business bases, never rental, capital or other income (§11(1)).
- The personal allowance and the spouse allowance are tested on the tax base from §5 and §6(1),(2) income. A taxpayer who at the start of 2026 receives an old-age, early, service or similar foreign pension gets no personal allowance if the pension for the year, including the 13th pension, exceeds the allowance; otherwise the allowance is cut to the difference (§11(6)).
- The spouse allowance needs a spouse living with the taxpayer who cared for a minor child, received a care allowance, was a registered jobseeker, or is disabled (§11(4)). The spouse's own income is net of their contributions. Months count only if the conditions held at the start of the month (§11(5)).
- **DDS/PEPP pension contributions:** deduct the taxpayer's own contributions demonstrably paid in the year, with one EUR 180 annual cap across the qualifying products, including qualifying equivalent foreign products (§11(8)/(9)). For DDS, the participant contract must have been concluded after 31 December 2013, or amended to cancel its benefit plan; a qualifying PEPP contract is the alternative. The taxpayer must also have no other DDS participant contract that fails that condition (§11(10)). Thus EUR 240 eligible DDS payments plus EUR 60 eligible PEPP payments give a combined EUR 180 deduction, rather than EUR 180 for each product; retaining another non-qualifying DDS contract prevents the claim. If a statutory early withdrawal is paid after earlier DDS deductions, add back the previously deducted DDS contributions to the tax base within the three tax periods after the withdrawal year (§11(11)). A 2026 early withdrawal with EUR 360 previously deducted therefore requires EUR 360 added back by the end of tax year 2029. Keep the payment records, every DDS contract/amendment, PEPP contract and past deduction/withdrawal history ([ITA §11(8)–(11)](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2003/595/20260101.html#paragraf-11)).
- Allowances come off the employment base first, and only the rest comes off the business base (§11(12)).
disposition: Existing allowance sequence verbatim;R06 DDS/PEPP gate andclawback appended

baseline_text: **Rental (§6(3)) and other income (§8).** Income minus proven expenses. Rental income and occasional income are exempt up to EUR 500 in total (§9(1)(g)). Sales of property, movable things, options, securities, shares in an s.r.o. and crypto-assets (§8(1)(b)-(f),(t)) are taxed on the gain. A loss on one type is ignored (§8(2)). Several sales are exempt if held long enough, for example listed securities held over a year (§9(1)(k)). These gains are taxed in base (a) on the bands.
closest_final_text: **Rental (§6(3)) and other income (§8).** Start with the actual income and supported category-specific expenses. Under §9(1)(g), rental and §8(1)(a) occasional income share EUR 500 of annual income exemption. If they exceed that amount, include only the excess and reduce related expenses in the same taxable-income/total-income proportion. For a rental-only case with EUR 6,000 receipts, EUR 2,000 expenses and the whole EUR 500 available, taxable receipts are EUR 5,500; allowable expenses are `2,000 × 5,500 / 6,000`, approximately EUR 1,833.33, leaving approximately EUR 3,666.67 before the applicable filing-rounding steps. Full EUR 2,000 expenses cannot be deducted against the reduced receipts, and rental expenses cannot create a rental loss (§6(6)). Where qualifying §8(1)(d)–(f) option/security/share disposals also occur, §9(1)(i) applies to their proceeds less statutory disposal costs, with its business-asset and specified noncash-share exclusions; the exemptions under (g) and (i) together cannot exceed EUR 500. Do not give each category another EUR 500. Sales of property, movable things, options, securities, shares in an s.r.o. and crypto-assets (§8(1)(b)–(f),(t)) retain their actual gain/exemption rules; a loss on one type is ignored (§8(2)). The §9(1)(k) securities exemption requires more than one year since acquisition **and** more than one year between regulated-market admission and sale, excluding business assets and the specified §9(1)(p)/§5(7)(q) noncash-share cases, subject to §52zzz(3)'s acquisition-after-2023 transition. These taxable gains enter base (a) on the bands ([ITA §§6, 8, 9 and 52zzz](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2003/595/20260101.html)).

baseline_text: **Capital income (§7).** Slovak interest is taxed by withholding under §43 and stays out of the return (§7(3)). Foreign interest and similar income go in a special base taxed at 19% (§15(a)(4)). Dividends from a Slovak company are taxed by withholding. Foreign dividends go in a special base at 7%, or 35% from a non-cooperating state (§51e, §15(a)(5),(6)).
closest_final_text: **Capital income (§7).** Ordinary Slovak bank interest is taxed finally by withholding under §43 and stays out of the return (§7(3)); ordinary foreign bank interest enters the §7 special base at 19% (§15(a)(4)). Identify the instrument before applying that rule. Non-exempt yields on Slovak government bonds/treasury bills and bonds/bills issued by another EU/EEA state enter the **gross, no-expense-deduction §51ea special base at 13%** in 2026 (§15(a)(7)); the temporary 16% rate was for 2025 payments only (§52zzzc(3)). Section 43(3)(v)'s separate 13% withholding route concerns recipients not established or created for business; it is not a blanket withholding rule for individual bondholders. Qualifying Slovak retail government bonds (štátne dlhopisy pre občanov) and equivalent EU/EEA-state retail bonds have exempt yields **and sale income**, unless they are or were the taxpayer's business assets (§9(1)(r)). A non-exempt government-bond coupon of EUR 1,000 therefore gives EUR 130 tax before foreign-tax relief, ordinary foreign bank interest of EUR 1,000 gives EUR 190, and a qualifying non-business retail-bond coupon of EUR 1,000 gives zero. Do not extend the coupon special base to every bond sale ([ITA §§9,15,43,51ea,52zzzc](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2003/595/20260101.html)). Dividends from a Slovak company are taxed by withholding. For ordinary foreign profit dividends, select the profit period before the rate: 7% for periods beginning in 2017–2023 and from 1 January 2025, but 10% for periods beginning in 2024, even when all are received in 2026. The 35% non-cooperating-state rule is separate (§51e, §15(a)(5),(6), §52zi(5), §52zzz(4), §52zzzb(5)). For EUR 10,000 gross, those ordinary domestic-law rates give EUR 700 or EUR 1,000 before applicable foreign-tax relief. Pre-2017 profit distributions need their historical regime and are not assigned either rate here.

baseline_text:
**Credits.** From the tax computed:
- **Child tax bonus (§33).** EUR 100 a month for each child under 15 and EUR 50 a month for each child aged 15 to 18, for each month at whose start the conditions were met (§33(1),(5)). The child lives in the taxpayer's household, and the taxpayer needs employment or business income. The total is capped at a percentage of the employment or business partial base, or their sum, taken before allowances (§33(6)); the Financial Administration's worked return uses that base. If that base exceeds EUR 27,432, the bonus for each child falls by one tenth of the excess (§33(11)). Only one parent claims (§33(4)). If the bonus exceeds the tax, the difference is paid out (§33(7)). The taxpayer must have at least 90% of income from Slovak sources (§33(9)).
- **Mortgage interest bonus** for borrowers aged 18 to 35 at application (§33a). The conditions differ for loan contracts made up to 31 December 2023 and after; check them in the law before claiming it.
closest_final_text: Use the §5 and §6(1),(2) partial bases before allowances, or their sum B, for the 29%/36%/43%/50%/57%/64% cap for one/two/three/four/five/six-or-more children. If the eligible child count changes, split the cap by the number of months at each child count and sum those proportional entitlements (§33(6),(10)). Above B = EUR 27,432 in 2026, reduce each child's entitlement by one tenth of the excess; for part-year eligibility apply the corresponding eligible-month share, without creating a negative bonus (§33(5),(11)). The tax return can augment B by the other eligible household person's §5/§6(1),(2) base when the claimant lacks the base for the full bonus, using only the proportional months at whose start the other person qualified if they qualified for only part of the year. This is a credit calculation, not a transfer of taxable income; test **both the percentage cap and the high-base taper on augmented B** (§33(8)). The claimant must have at least 90% of all income from Slovak taxable sources, and so must the other person if their base is added (§33(9)). Claim the excess bonus over tax as a payout (§33(7)).

baseline_text: ## Who this applies to
closest_final_text: ## Who this applies to

baseline_text:
- **Slovak-resident legal persons**: a company with its seat or place of effective management in Slovakia (§ 2(d) second point). Typical clients: s.r.o., a.s., cooperatives. They are taxed on worldwide income.
- **Non-resident legal persons** with Slovak-source income (§ 16), in particular a permanent establishment in Slovakia. A registered permanent establishment files a DPPO return like a resident. Slovak income with no permanent establishment is mostly taxed by withholding (§ 43); see "Cross-border points".
- **Non-profit bodies** (§ 12(3)) are taxed only on part of their income. Not covered here.

baseline_text: ## The taxable base
closest_final_text: ## The taxable base

baseline_text: **Start from accounting profit.** A company that keeps double-entry books starts from the profit or loss in its statutory accounts (Slovak GAAP or IFRS), then adds back and deducts the items the Act lists (§ 17). The result, less tax losses, is the base the rate applies to.
closest_final_text: **Start from accounting profit.** A company that keeps double-entry books starts from the profit or loss in its statutory accounts (Slovak GAAP or IFRS), then adds back and deducts the items the Act lists (§ 17). The result, less tax losses, is the base the rate applies to.

baseline_text:
**Common add-backs.**
- Expenses that are not tax expenses under § 21, such as representation (entertainment) costs, and fines and penalties imposed by public bodies.
- Expenses deductible only when paid (§ 17(19)). Among them: rent and royalties; marketing and market studies; commissions; legal and advisory services under CPA codes 69.1, 69.2, 70.1 and 70.22; contractual penalties and late payment interest owed by the company; payments to a person in a non-cooperating state once withholding duties are met. If they are booked in 2026 and paid in 2027, they come into the 2027 base.
- From 1 January 2026, VAT that a VAT payer has no right to deduct is not a tax expense, and on tangible assets it is not part of the entry price (§ 52zzzk, inserted by Act No. 261/2025). If the split between business and non-business use of the asset later changes, that VAT is not taken into the base either. Check this for any VAT-registered client with exempt supplies or blocked input VAT.
- Accounting depreciation above tax depreciation.
- Interest caught by § 21a or § 17k (see below).
closest_final_text:
**Common add-backs.**
- Expenses that are not tax expenses under § 21, such as representation (entertainment) costs, and fines and penalties imposed by public bodies.
- Expenses deductible only when paid (§ 17(19)). Among them: rent and royalties; marketing and market studies; commissions; legal and advisory services under CPA codes 69.1, 69.2, 70.1 and 70.22; contractual penalties and late payment interest owed by the company; payments to a person in a non-cooperating state once withholding duties are met. If they are booked in 2026 and paid in 2027, they come into the 2027 base.
- From 1 January 2026, the nondeductible-VAT rule in § 52zzzk applies specifically to VAT restricted under [VAT Act § 85n](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-85n), as its footnote 161 states. That restricted vehicle-related VAT is not a tax expense and, for the specified tangible vehicle, is not part of its tax entry price; the linked later business/private-use VAT change is outside the income-tax base. This is not a general disallowance of all VAT that an exempt or mixed business cannot recover. Ordinary nondeductible VAT and coefficient VAT follow § 19(3)(k): eligible expense VAT can be a tax expense; VAT included in tangible/intangible asset entry price under § 25(5)(b)/(c) instead follows the asset treatment. For example, outside the § 85n restriction, a qualifying machine costing EUR 10,000 plus EUR 2,300 VAT, with 60% VAT recovery, has EUR 920 nondeductible VAT and tax entry price EUR 10,920, not an automatic EUR 920 add-back ([ITA §§ 19, 25 and 52zzzk](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2003/595/20260101.html)).
- Accounting depreciation above tax depreciation.
- Interest caught by § 21a or § 17k (see below).

baseline_text: **Common deductions.** Income not subject to tax, such as most dividends (§ 12(7)(c), below); tax depreciation above accounting depreciation; the R&D super-deduction (§ 30c: 100% of R&D costs, plus 100% of the increase in the two-year average of R&D costs over the average of the two prior periods) and the investment deduction (§ 30e) where the conditions are met.
closest_final_text: **Common deductions.** Income not subject to tax, such as most dividends (§ 12(7)(c), below); tax depreciation above accounting depreciation; the R&D super-deduction (§ 30c: 100% of R&D costs, plus 100% of the increase in the two-year average of R&D costs over the average of the two prior periods) and the investment deduction (§ 30e) where the conditions are met.

baseline_text: **Depreciation (§ 26 and § 27).** Tangible assets go into one of seven groups. Straight-line annual depreciation (§ 27) is entry price divided by the period. In the first year only the months from the month the asset is put into use count. Assets in groups 2 and 3 may instead be depreciated by the accelerated method (§ 28); the method is chosen per new asset and cannot be changed (§ 26(3)). **Interest: two separate limits.**

baseline_text:
- **Return.** The DPPO return is due within three calendar months after the end of the tax period: 31 March 2027 for calendar 2026 (§ 49(2)). Tax is payable by the same date.
- **Extension by notice.** A notice filed with the tax office before the deadline moves it by up to three whole calendar months, to 30 June 2027 for calendar 2026. The new date is the end of the month the company names. If the company has foreign-source income, the move is up to six months, to 30 September 2027 (§ 49(3)(a) and (b)). Tax is due on the new date. Companies in liquidation or bankruptcy apply instead, at least 15 days before the deadline (§ 49(3)(c)).
- **Form.** On 23 October 2026 the Financial Administration's return page names form MF/012187/2025-721, with filing notes for periods whose deadline falls after 31 December 2025. It has 15 pages and at least five annexes even when blank. Before filing the 2026 return, check that page for a newer form.
- **Electronic filing.** A legal person entered in the commercial register, and any VAT payer, must file electronically (Tax Procedure Code § 14(1)(a)). Some annexes may be sent in other ways, but the VII-part annex and the § 13a, § 13b, § 30ca and § 30e annexes form part of the return.
- **Minimum tax** is payable by the return deadline (§ 46b(4)).
- **Advances in 2026 (§ 42).** The tax that sets them (§ 42(6)) is the tax on the base after losses, at the § 15 rate shown in the previous period's return, less reliefs under the Act. It is the computed tax, not the minimum tax. Based on the 2025 tax:
  - above EUR 16,600: monthly, 1/12 of that tax, by the end of each month;
  - above EUR 5,000 up to EUR 16,600: quarterly, 1/4, by the end of each calendar quarter (or quarter of the fiscal year);
  - up to EUR 5,000: none, unless the tax office orders them.
  Until the deadline for the 2025 return, advances follow the last known tax, from the 2024 return (§ 42(7)). A company formed during the year (other than by merger or division) pays no advances in its first period (§ 42(4)). A company filing its first return pays no advances until that return is due, then makes up the advances that fell due by the end of the following month (§ 42(8)).
- **Financial transaction tax.** Separate from CIT, Act No. 279/2024 Coll. taxes financial transactions. Its § 6 rates from 1 January 2026: 0.4%, at most EUR 40 per transaction; 0.8% on cash withdrawals; EUR 2 per payment card. This skill does not cover it beyond this pointer.

baseline_text:
- **Withholding on payments abroad (§ 43).** Tax is withheld at 19% on Slovak-source income of a non-resident without a registered permanent establishment, such as royalties, interest and certain services. The rate is 35% where the payee is in a non-cooperating state. A treaty or the EU Interest and Royalties Directive can reduce or remove it. For the detailed rules see [sk-cross-border](sk-cross-border.md).
- **Dividends paid abroad.** A dividend paid by a Slovak company to a company is not subject to tax (§ 12(7)(c)). The exception is a recipient company that is a taxpayer of a non-cooperating state (§ 12(7)(c)(1)). That dividend is withheld under § 43(2) (§ 16(1)(e) point 9) at 35% (§ 43(1)(c)).
- **Exit tax (§ 17f).** Moving assets, the seat or the business abroad creates a special base taxed at 21%.
- **Permanent establishments.** The § 21a and § 17k limits and the rate bands apply to a non-resident's Slovak permanent establishment as they do to a resident company.
- **Pillar Two.** Act No. 507/2023 Coll. on top-up tax applies to Slovak members of a multinational or large domestic group whose ultimate parent's consolidated accounts show annual revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000 in at least two of the four preceding periods (§ 3(1)(a)). Those groups also need a top-up tax computation. Not covered here.

1. Taxable revenue for the period. It sets the rate band (EUR 100,000 and EUR 5,000,000), the minimum tax band, and micro-taxpayer status (EUR 60,000).
2. The tax period: calendar or fiscal year, and whether it is the company's first period (no minimum tax, no advances).
3. Any transaction with a related person in the period. It removes micro-taxpayer status and brings in § 21a for related-party interest.
4. Unused tax losses by year, and any minimum tax paid in 2023 to 2025 still to be credited.
5. Unpaid year-end items in the § 17(19) list (rent, royalties, advisory and legal fees, penalties), and whether the company recovers its input VAT in full.
6. Foreign income or payments to non-residents, and whether any counterparty is in a non-cooperating state.

baseline_text: ## Who this applies to
closest_final_text: ## Who this applies to

baseline_text: **Employers.** Any person or company that pays an employee is a social insurance payer and deducts the employee's share (Act 461/2003 §§ 128, 141(2)). It is also a health insurance payer and computes and pays health advances for each employee (Act 580/2004 §16(2)(a), (c), (4)). An employer resident in Slovakia, or a foreign one with a Slovak branch, is the tax payer (platiteľ dane) and withholds the monthly tax advance (Act 595/2003 §35(1)).
closest_final_text: **Employers.** Any person or company that pays an employee is a social insurance payer and deducts the employee's share (Act 461/2003 §§ 128, 141(2)). It is also a health insurance payer and computes and pays health advances for each employee (Act 580/2004 §16(2)(a), (c), (4)). An employer resident in Slovakia, or a foreign one with a Slovak branch, is the tax payer (platiteľ dane) and withholds the monthly tax advance (Act 595/2003 §35(1)).

baseline_text: **Employees.** People in an employment relationship (pracovný pomer) and people on work agreements (dohody). There is no minimum assessment base for an employee's social insurance: the base is the pay actually accounted (Act 461/2003 §138(1); Sociálna poisťovňa, 2026 tables, note 1). The employer must still pay at least the minimum wage under labour law: EUR 915 a month from 1 January 2026 ([Ministry of Labour, minimum wage 2026](https://www.employment.gov.sk/sk/uvodna-stranka/informacie-media/aktuality/historicky-narast-minimalnej-mzdy-je-realitou-roku-2026-je-minimalna-mzda-vo-vyske-915-eur.html)).

There is no minimum assessment base for an employee's social insurance: the base is the pay actually accounted (Act 461/2003 §138(1); Sociálna poisťovňa, 2026 tables, note 1). The employer must still pay at least the minimum wage under labour law: EUR 915 a month from 1 January 2026 ([Ministry of Labour, minimum wage 2026](https://www.employment.gov.sk/sk/uvodna-stranka/informacie-media/aktuality/historicky-narast-minimalnej-mzdy-je-realitou-roku-2026-je-minimalna-mzda-vo-vyske-915-eur.html)).

baseline_text:
**Self-employed (SZČO).** From 1 January 2026 a person aged 18 or over is an SZČO for social insurance if they hold a licence to do business or, by an honest declaration, carry on self-employed work that needs no licence (for example an artist or author). Income no longer decides this status (Sociálna poisťovňa, changes from 1 January 2026, item 22).
- **New entrants** (no licence in the last 60 months) become compulsorily insured from the first day of the sixth calendar month after the month the licence starts.
- **Returning entrants** (a licence ended less than 60 months ago) are insured from the day the licence starts.
- Insurance now lasts until the licence ends. The old income test at 1 July no longer ends it.
- **Transition:** to 30 June 2026 an SZČO who held a licence before 1 January 2026 stays under the old rules. Under those rules insurance started on 1 July 2025 (1 October 2025 with an extended tax deadline) if 2024 income was above EUR 8,580 (Sociálna poisťovňa, 2026 tables, note 3).
closest_final_text: **Not covered here.** Voluntary insurance (dobrovoľne poistená osoba), the special scheme for municipal police, and health insurance on dividends. See `slovakia-pit` for an SZČO's annual return.

baseline_text: **Employee social base.** Pay from the work, except income that is not taxable or is exempt from income tax, and except employer contributions to supplementary pension saving (Act 461/2003 §138(1)). A profit share paid to an employee who holds no capital is included. The base is capped at EUR 16,764 a month; employer accident insurance runs on the full pay (§138(10)). From 2026 the employee and employer pay social insurance on any pay accounted during sickness, maternity or care leave. The old exclusion periods are gone for employees (Sociálna poisťovňa, changes from 1 January 2026, item 26). Where someone has several jobs, social contributions run from the highest base down (§138(12)).

baseline_text: ## Cross-border points
closest_final_text: ## Cross-border points

baseline_text:
- **EU coordination.** Within the EU, EEA and Switzerland a person is subject to one country's social security law at a time (Regulation 883/2004 Art. 11(1)). A worker posted from Slovakia for work expected to last up to 24 months stays under Slovak law (Art. 12(1)) and carries an A1 form issued by Sociálna poisťovňa. A worker posted to Slovakia with a foreign A1 pays no Slovak social insurance.
- **Foreign employer.** A foreign employer with no Slovak branch is not the tax payer. A resident employee pays the tax advances themselves by the end of the next month (Act 595/2003 §35(10)). A non-resident does the same under §35(11), from the start of the stay if the contract shows more than 183 days.
- **Pay taxed abroad.** The employer withholds no advance on pay that is taxed abroad (Act 595/2003 §35(8)). The tax bonus needs at least 90% of total income from Slovak sources (§33(9)). Treaty conditions and documents are in `sk-cross-border`.
closest_final_text:
- **EU coordination and posting.** Within the EU, EEA and Switzerland a person covered by the coordination rules is subject to one country's social security law at a time. The ordinary rule is the country of work (Regulation 883/2004 Art.11(1), (3)(a)). An employee posted from Slovakia stays under Slovak law under Art.12(1) only if the expected posting does not exceed 24 months, the employer normally carries out substantial business in Slovakia beyond internal administration, the employee works on its behalf and the direct employment relationship continues throughout, and the employee is not sent to replace another posted person. A short assignment alone does not satisfy those conditions. Keep evidence of the employer's real Slovak activity and turnover, contracts and workforce, and its continuing authority over the nature of work, pay, discipline and termination. For an employee recruited for posting, also establish the immediately preceding Slovak coverage; the current application asks about at least one month.
  The employer and employee apply sufficiently before departure to the Sociálna poisťovňa branch holding the employer's register. That branch checks the conditions and issues PD A1, which the employer gives to the employee. The current nine-page [official application and instructions](https://socpoist.sk/api/idsp/download/cc10770f-2166-45b6-a4c4-60423faec92a) directly confirm the issuer and evidence. Its narrowly described objective-replacement cases (for example death or long illness, with aggregate posting no longer than 24 months) need the branch's assessment; routine rotation on the same job is not a fresh posting. Keep the conditions satisfied throughout and notify changes. An expected posting beyond 24 months requires the separate Art.16 agreed-exception route rather than an assumed Art.12 entitlement. Regular work in two or more states instead requires an Art.13 applicable-legislation determination; do not classify it automatically as successive postings. A valid foreign A1 establishing foreign legislation for a worker posted to Slovakia means no Slovak social insurance for its covered period (Arts.11–13; official application, pp.5–9).
- **Foreign employer.** A registered Slovak branch is not the sole wage-tax payer test. Apply ITA §48(1) first: a foreign person can be a payer because of a Slovak permanent establishment or employment in Slovakia for more than 183 days, continuously or cumulatively in any twelve consecutive months, with the specified §16(1)(c) service-provider and diplomatic-office qualifications; §48(1)(b) supplies its separate source-income ground. In an economic-employer case under §5(4), apply §48(2)'s special allocation: the foreign person is not the payer, except that a foreign person with a Slovak organisational branch is a payer to the extent of the wages it provides. Only after establishing that the employer is not a payer apply §35(10)/(11): a resident employee pays their own advances by the end of the following month, and a non-resident follows §35(11), including its from-start treatment where the contract shows more than 183 days. Retain the PE, actual employment-day history, contract and economic-employer facts ([ITA §§35 and 48](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2003/595/20260101.html#paragraf-48)).
- **Pay taxed abroad.** The employer withholds no advance on pay that is taxed abroad (Act 595/2003 §35(8)). The tax bonus needs at least 90% of total income from Slovak sources (§33(9)). Treaty conditions and documents are in `sk-cross-border`.

baseline_text: ## Ask the client first
closest_final_text: ## Ask the client first

baseline_text:
1. **Contract type for each worker.** Employment contract, work agreement (dohoda) or self-employed. This changes the unemployment and support rates, the EUR 200 deduction and the health deductible amount.
2. **Has the employee signed the tax declaration with you, and which children (with ages) are claimed?** Only one employer gives the EUR 497.23 allowance and the tax bonus.
3. **Disability, pension or second-pillar status.** Disability halves the health rates; a pensioner pays no disability or unemployment insurance; a saver's 4% goes to the pension fund.
4. **Your payday.** Social and health payments fall due on it; the tax advance 5 days later.
5. **For an SZČO: the date the licence started, any licence that ended in the last 60 months, the last two returns (income, tax base, contributions deducted) and any extended filing deadline.** These set the start date and both bases.
6. **Any work abroad, A1 form or foreign employer.** This changes who collects.
closest_final_text:
1. **Contract type for each worker.** Employment contract, work agreement (dohoda) or self-employed. This changes the unemployment and support rates, the EUR 200 deduction and the health deductible amount.
2. **Has the employee signed the tax declaration with you, and which children (with ages) are claimed?** Only one employer gives the EUR 497.23 allowance and the tax bonus.
3. **Exact disability/pension category, award date, retirement age and second-pillar status.** The health disability rates need the statutory qualifying status. Social disability premiums do not apply after an old-age or early-old-age pension award, or to a service-pension recipient who has reached retirement age; the employer follows the same exclusion (§128(3)). Unemployment insurance separately excludes old-age/early-old-age recipients, disability-pension recipients with more than 70% loss of earning capacity, and disability-pension recipients who reached retirement age (§19(3)(b)). Do not treat every pensioner as exempt from both branches. Check a work agreement's actual §4 insurance category rather than automatically applying the ordinary employee total; a second-pillar saver's 4% contribution is allocated to their pension fund ([Social Insurance Act §§4, 19 and 128](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2003/461/20260901.html)).
4. **Your payday.** Social and health payments fall due on it; the tax advance 5 days later.
5. **For an SZČO: the date the licence started, any licence that ended in the last 60 months, the last two returns (income, tax base, contributions deducted) and any extended filing deadline.** These set the start date and both bases.
6. **Any work abroad, A1 form or foreign employer, including a Slovak PE, branch, employment days in each rolling twelve-month period and economic-employer arrangements.** These facts determine the applicable country and wage-tax payer.

baseline_text: # Slovakia: cross-border income tax (2026)
closest_final_text: # Slovakia: cross-border income tax (2026)

baseline_text: This skill covers what happens in Slovak income tax when income, people or companies cross the border. The law is the Income Tax Act, Act No. 595/2003 Coll. (zákon o dani z príjmov, "ZDP"), in the version in force from 1 January 2026 to 30 December 2026. Procedure, penalties and interest come from the Tax Procedure Code, Act No. 563/2009 Coll. (daňový poriadok). The authority is the Financial Administration (Finančná správa SR). The currency is the euro.

baseline_text: **What changed for 2026.** The 2025 consolidation package, Act No. 261/2025 Coll. of 24 September 2025, did not change the withholding rules (§ 43) or the security rules (§ 44). It did change the individual rate bands to 19%, 25%, 30% and 35% for 2026 (§ 15 letter a), § 52zzzj), cut the personal allowance bands, and replaced the company minimum tax scale (§ 46b(2)). The 7% dividend rate and the 10% / 21% / 24% company rates were already in force from 2025. Set against the version in force from 1 December 2025, the 2026 text of § 2, § 13, § 16, § 17f, § 17g, § 44 and § 45 is unchanged. In § 43 only the content of the withholding notice changed (§ 43(11)): for each non-resident recipient it now gives the income type (for § 16(1)(e) points 1, 2, 4, 9 and 11), the amount, the rate, the recipient's address and its foreign tax number.

baseline_text: ## Who this applies to
closest_final_text: ## Who this applies to

baseline_text: ### Individuals
closest_final_text: ### Individuals

baseline_text: An individual has unlimited tax liability in Slovakia (is resident) if they have permanent residence (trvalý pobyt), a home (bydlisko), or habitually stay here (§ 2 letter d) point 1 ZDP).
closest_final_text: An individual has unlimited tax liability in Slovakia (is resident) if they have permanent residence (trvalý pobyt), a home (bydlisko), or habitually stay here (§ 2 letter d) point 1 ZDP).

baseline_text:
- **Home.** A person has a home here if they have accommodation that is not only occasional, and their personal and economic ties show an intention to stay there permanently (§ 2 letter d) point 1a).
- **183 days.** A person habitually stays here if present for at least 183 days in the calendar year, in one stretch or several. Every day started counts (§ 2 letter d) point 1b).
- **Study or medical treatment only.** A person here only to study or for medical treatment is not resident (§ 2 letter e) point 2).
- **Treaty tie-breaker.** A person who is resident under Slovak law but resident in the other state under a tax treaty has limited liability (§ 2 letter e) point 1).
closest_final_text:
- **Home.** A person has a home here if they have accommodation that is not only occasional, and their personal and economic ties show an intention to stay there permanently (§ 2 letter d) point 1a).
- **183 days.** A person habitually stays here if present for at least 183 days in the calendar year, in one stretch or several. Every day started counts (§ 2 letter d) point 1b).
- **Study or medical treatment only.** A person here only to study or for medical treatment is not resident (§ 2 letter e) point 2).
- **Treaty tie-breaker.** A person who is resident under Slovak law but resident in the other state under a tax treaty has limited liability (§ 2 letter e) point 1).

baseline_text: ### Companies
closest_final_text: ### Companies

baseline_text: A legal person is resident if its seat or its place of effective management is in Slovakia. The place of effective management is where the key management and business decisions for the entity as a whole are made, even if that address is not in the commercial register (§ 2 letter d) point 2). A company that a treaty treats as resident in the other state has limited liability (§ 2 letter e) point 3).
closest_final_text: A legal person is resident if its seat or its place of effective management is in Slovakia. The place of effective management is where the key management and business decisions for the entity as a whole are made, even if that address is not in the commercial register (§ 2 letter d) point 2). A company that a treaty treats as resident in the other state has limited liability (§ 2 letter e) point 3).

baseline_text: ### Scope of tax
closest_final_text: ### Scope of tax

baseline_text:
- Residents are taxed on Slovak and foreign income (§ 2 letter f)).
- Non-residents are taxed only on Slovak-source income listed in § 16 (§ 2 letter g)).
closest_final_text:
- Residents are taxed on Slovak and foreign income (§ 2 letter f)).
- Non-residents are taxed only on Slovak-source income listed in § 16 (§ 2 letter g)).

baseline_text: ### Who acts
closest_final_text: ### Who acts

baseline_text:
- **Slovak payers** (companies, sole traders, permanent establishments) paying non-residents. They withhold tax (§ 43) or a security deduction (§ 44) and they are liable if they do not (§ 43(12), § 44(6)).
- **Non-residents** with Slovak income: employees, service providers, sellers of Slovak property or shares, and foreign companies with a Slovak permanent establishment.
- **Residents** with foreign income who need double tax relief (§ 45).
- **Companies** moving assets, business or their residence out of Slovakia (§ 17f, exit tax).

baseline_text: ### Permanent establishment (stála prevádzkareň, § 16(2))
closest_final_text: ### Permanent establishment (stála prevádzkareň, § 16(2))

baseline_text: A permanent establishment is a fixed place through which the non-resident carries on its activity in Slovakia: a branch, office, workshop, worksite, point of sale, technical equipment, or a place of extraction. A place is fixed if it is used continuously or repeatedly.
closest_final_text: A permanent establishment is a fixed place through which the non-resident carries on its activity in Slovakia: a branch, office, workshop, worksite, point of sale, technical equipment, or a place of extraction. A place is fixed if it is used continuously or repeatedly.

baseline_text:
- A one-off activity creates a permanent establishment only after more than six months in any 12 months. A building site or construction or assembly project is one only if the activity of the non-resident or its related persons there lasts more than six months.
- Services provided in Slovakia by the non-resident or its staff create one after more than 183 days in any 12 months.
- Repeated intermediation of transport or accommodation, including through a digital platform, counts as a fixed place.
- A dependent agent is one: a person acting on the non-resident's instructions who habitually negotiates, concludes or arranges contracts, or plays the principal role leading to contracts the non-resident concludes without material change, in the non-resident's name or for its property or services.
closest_final_text:
- A one-off activity creates a permanent establishment only after more than six months in any 12 months. A building site or construction or assembly project is one only if the activity of the non-resident or its related persons there lasts more than six months.
- Services provided in Slovakia by the non-resident or its staff create one after more than 183 days in any 12 months.
- Repeated intermediation of transport or accommodation, including through a digital platform, counts as a fixed place.
- A dependent agent is one: a person acting on the non-resident's instructions who habitually negotiates, concludes or arranges contracts, or plays the principal role leading to contracts the non-resident concludes without material change, in the non-resident's name or for its property or services.

baseline_text: Income of a registered permanent establishment is not withheld at source (§ 43(2)). It is declared in a return and taxed at the normal rates.
closest_final_text: Income of a registered permanent establishment is not withheld at source (§ 43(2)). It is declared in a return and taxed at the normal rates.

It removes states on the EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions as at 1 January, and states with no corporate income tax or a zero rate.

baseline_text:

baseline_text: ### Double tax relief for residents (§ 45)
closest_final_text: ### Double tax relief for residents (§ 45)

baseline_text:
- **Treaty state, credit method.** Foreign tax is credited up to the lower of (a) the tax the treaty allows the other state to charge and (b) the Slovak tax on the foreign income. The limit is Slovak tax times the foreign base as a percentage of the total base. For an individual the total base is taken before the § 11 personal allowances. Only tax on income included in this year's base can be credited (§ 45(1)).
- **Treaty state, exemption method.** The foreign base is left out of the Slovak base (§ 45(1)).
- **Employment income.** It is exempt if taxed abroad and it comes from a non-treaty state, from EU institutions, or from a treaty state where exemption gives a better result than the treaty method (§ 45(3)).
- **Different foreign tax year.** If the foreign tax receipt is not available by the filing deadline, the return shows the expected foreign income and tax (§ 45(2)).

baseline_text: ## Deadlines and filing
closest_final_text: ## Deadlines and filing

baseline_text:
- **Withholding tax:** the payer pays it to the tax office by the 15th of each month for the previous month, and files the notice of withholding (oznámenie o zrazení a odvedení dane) by the same date (§ 43(11)).
- **Security deduction:** paid by the 15th of each month for the previous month, with the notice on the official form (§ 44(3)).
- **Income tax return:** within three months after the end of the tax period, so 31 March 2027 for 2026. The tax is due by the same date (§ 49(2)).
- **Extension:** a notice filed before the deadline extends it by up to three whole months, or up to six whole months if the income includes foreign-source income. The tax is then due by the new date (§ 49(3)(a) and (b)).
- **Exit tax:** due with the return, or in instalments if allowed (§ 17g(1) to (3)).
- **Recipient's challenge:** a recipient who doubts a withholding may ask the payer for an explanation within 12 months; the payer has 30 days to reply and correct it (§ 43a(1)).

baseline_text: ## Cross-border points
closest_final_text: ## Cross-border points

baseline_text:
- **Treaties override domestic rates.** A treaty can lower or remove Slovak withholding (§ 1(2)). The Ministry of Finance list valid from 1 January 2026 names 71 states with a Slovak tax treaty, including Kyrgyzstan, whose treaty applies from 1 January 2026. Read the treaty in force for the year of payment for the rate.
- **Beneficial owner.** The beneficial owner is the person who receives the income for its own benefit and can use it freely, or its permanent establishment. An intermediary is not (§ 2 letter af)). A payer that cannot show the beneficial owner applies 35% (§ 43(25), § 44(7)).
- **Reporting the recipient.** The withholding notice names each non-resident recipient, with its address and foreign tax number, and splits royalties, rent of movables, dividends and similar income by type (§ 43(11)(b)).

- **Transfer pricing** between related parties, including a head office and its permanent establishment (§ 2 letter r)), is out of scope here.

baseline_text: ## Who this applies to
closest_final_text: ## Who this applies to

baseline_text: **Any taxpayer that is a dependent person and has a significant controlled transaction.** The rule in ITA § 17(5) applies to companies and to individuals with business income under § 6, residents and non-residents.
closest_final_text: **Any taxpayer that is a dependent person and has a significant controlled transaction.** The rule in ITA § 17(5) applies to companies and to individuals with business income under § 6, residents and non-residents.

baseline_text: **Dependent persons (závislé osoby), ITA § 2(n) to (r):**
closest_final_text: **Dependent persons (závislé osoby), ITA § 2(n) to (r):**

baseline_text:
- **Close persons** (blízke osoby, Civil Code §§ 116 and 117) (§ 2(n)(1)).
- **Economically, personally or otherwise linked persons** (§ 2(n)(2)):
  - **Economic link** (§ 2(o)(1)): a direct, indirect or derived indirect share of at least 25% of the registered capital, of the voting rights or of the profit. An indirect share is the product of the direct shares. A derived indirect share is the sum of indirect shares; above 50%, every person in the chain counts as economically linked whatever its own share. Persons acting together on votes or capital count as holding all of it. Shares of close persons are added together, and 25% in total makes them linked.
  - **Personal link** (§ 2(o)(2)): members of the statutory, supervisory or similar bodies of a legal person, in relation to that legal person. Persons under the control or management of the same person, or of its close person, are linked to each other (§ 2(o)).
  - **Other link** (§ 2(p)): a legal or similar relationship set up mainly to reduce the tax base or increase a tax loss.
- **Members of a consolidated group** for consolidation purposes under Accounting Act § 22 (§ 2(n)(3)).
- **Permanent establishments** (§ 2(r)): a resident and its foreign PEs, a non-resident and its Slovak PE, PEs of the same taxpayer, and PEs of linked taxpayers all count as economically linked.

baseline_text: **Controlled transaction** (kontrolovaná transakcia, § 2(ab)): a legal or similar relationship between two or more dependent persons where at least one is an individual with § 6 business income or a legal person with taxable income from activity or from its assets. Two things are not controlled transactions: employment income under § 5, and the rent of a property outside business assets let to an individual for personal use. The real substance of the relationship counts.
closest_final_text: **Controlled transaction** (kontrolovaná transakcia, § 2(ab)): a legal or similar relationship between two or more dependent persons where at least one is an individual with § 6 business income or a legal person with taxable income from activity or from its assets. Two things are not controlled transactions: employment income under § 5, and the rent of a property outside business assets let to an individual for personal use. The real substance of the relationship counts.

baseline_text: **Significant controlled transaction** (§ 17(5)(a)): a transaction or group of transactions on which one or more dependent persons book taxable income or a tax expense above EUR 10,000 in the period, and any loan with principal above EUR 50,000. A loan above EUR 50,000 stays significant for its whole life, even after repayments take the balance below that (Financial Directorate, 12/PO/2026/IM, example 2). Transactions that are not significant are outside § 17(5) and are not reported in Table I.

baseline_text: ## The taxable base
closest_final_text: ## The taxable base

baseline_text: **The adjustment is one-way.** The base of a dependent person includes the difference by which prices or terms in significant controlled transactions depart from those between independent persons in comparable transactions. This applies only where the difference reduces the base or increases a tax loss (ITA § 17(5)(a)). The tax then follows at the taxpayer's own rate (§ 15).
closest_final_text: **The adjustment is one-way.** The base of a dependent person includes the difference by which prices or terms in significant controlled transactions depart from those between independent persons in comparable transactions. This applies only where the difference reduces the base or increases a tax loss (ITA § 17(5)(a)). The tax then follows at the taxpayer's own rate (§15). Recalculate that rate after the correction, using taxable revenue rather than the tax base. An income-side TP correction, such as increasing an undercharged sale, enters taxable revenue even if not booked; an expense-side addback, such as the excess management fee or royalty in the examples, increases the base without itself increasing taxable revenue. The Financial Directorate's [taxable-revenue methodology, p.2 item 3 and expense exclusions](https://www.financnasprava.sk/_img/pfsedit/Dokumenty_PFS/Zverejnovanie_dok/Dane/Metodicke_usmernenia/Priame_dane/2021/2021.02.11_18_DZPaU_2021_MU.pdf) explains that distinction; its historical rate and threshold are not the 2026 rates. Use current §15(b)(1): 10% through EUR 100,000 taxable revenue, 21% above that through EUR 5,000,000, and 24% above EUR 5,000,000, each on the entire ordinary base after loss relief. Compute extra tax as corrected tax less original tax, not invariably adjustment times the old rate. The exact-threshold values still take the lower rate.

baseline_text: ## Penalties and interest
closest_final_text: ## Penalties and interest

baseline_text:
- **Audit adjustment.** When the tax office raises tax in an assessment, the penalty is 3 times the ECB base rate a year, at least 10% a year, on the increase (TC § 155(1)(f), (5)). It runs for each day from the day after the return deadline until the 15-day window under § 16(9) after the audit starts closes. It is at least 1% of the amount and at most the amount (§ 155(2)). The ECB rate used is the one on the day the assessment is delivered (§ 155(7)). Paying the assessed amount within 15 days of delivery cuts the penalty to two thirds (§ 155(17)).
- **Doubled penalty for abuse.** Where the office adjusts under § 17(5)(a) and also applies the anti-abuse rule (ITA § 50a or TC § 3(6)), the penalty is doubled (ITA § 18a(1)). The doubling falls away if the taxpayer does not appeal and pays within the appeal period (§ 18a(2)).
- **APA requested.** Where the taxpayer asked for an APA and the office audits the period of the request or the two periods before it, an adjustment without abuse carries the lower penalty under TC § 155(1)(g) (ITA § 18a(3)).
- **Self-correction.** Tax disclosed in a supplementary return carries a penalty of the ECB base rate a year, at least 3% a year, on the difference (TC § 155(1)(g), (5)). It runs from the day after the return deadline until the supplementary return is filed (§ 155(2)). The rate is twice the ECB rate, at least 7%, if filed within 15 days after an audit starts (§ 155(1)(h)).
- **Documentation not handed over, or another non-monetary duty missed.** EUR 100 to EUR 10,000 (TC § 154(1)(j), § 155(1)(e)). The fine can be imposed again in the same amount if it did not lead to a remedy and the breach lasts (§ 155(16)). A tax office does not impose a fine set within a range for a first breach (§ 155(4)).
- **Late payment interest.** 4 times the ECB base rate on the day the arrears arose, at least 15% a year, for each day until payment, for at most 4 years (TC § 156(2)). Interest under EUR 5 is not charged (§ 156(6)(b)).
- **Country-by-country reporting.** Up to EUR 10,000 for not filing the report, and up to EUR 3,000 for a missed notice, both repeatable (Act 442/2012, § 22g(2)).
- **Time limit.** Tax can be assessed for 5 years from the end of the year in which the return was due. An audit report restarts the period, but never beyond 10 years (TC § 69(1) to (3)). Where a tax treaty is applied, the limit is 10 years (§ 69(5)).

baseline_text: ## Cross-border points
closest_final_text: ## Cross-border points

baseline_text:
- **Treaties and MAP.** A double taxation case from a TP adjustment can go to the mutual agreement procedure under the treaty's associated enterprises article, or to the EU Arbitration Convention 90/436/EEC. The documentation goes in with the request (ITA § 18(13)). EU disputes can also go under Act No. 11/2019 Z. z. on tax dispute resolution, and full documentation then applies to the transaction (guideline art. 3(1)(g)).
- **Corresponding adjustment after a foreign adjustment.** Allowed only where the other state has a tax treaty with Slovakia and its adjustment is arm's length (ITA § 17(6)). Full documentation applies (guideline art. 3(1)(f)).
- **Non-cooperative states.** A cross-border transaction with a resident of a non-cooperative state needs at least basic documentation whatever its size, and full documentation if it is material (guideline art. 3(1)(c), 3(2)(d)). The list of cooperating states is on the Ministry of Finance website (ITA § 2(x)).
- **Permanent establishments.** Head office dealings with a Slovak PE are controlled transactions (§ 2(r)) and go in Table I. Attribution of profit follows § 17(7).
- **Withholding.** Whether an adjusted amount paid abroad is treated as a dividend or other payment subject to withholding is not covered by this skill (see Not yet confirmed).

baseline_text: A Slovak s.r.o. has taxable revenue of EUR 3,000,000 in 2026, so its rate is 21%. It pays its Austrian parent a management fee of EUR 250,000 and deducts it in full. Its benchmark gives a range of independent fees with a median of EUR 180,000, and the fee sits above the range. In an audit that starts in June 2028, the office adjusts to the median.

baseline_text:
1. Documentation check: the fee is cross-border and above EUR 10,000, so it is significant. The company does not report under IFRS, claims no regional investment aid and Austria is not a non-cooperative state. The fee is below EUR 1,000,000 and the company's revenue is below EUR 8,000,000, so neither full nor basic documentation applies (guideline art. 3(1) and (2)). Table I in the 2026 return meets the duty (guideline art. 3(3)).

6. Had the office found it on audit instead, the 10% floor would apply over a longer period (TC § 155(1)(f)).

baseline_text: ## Who this applies to
closest_final_text: ## Who this applies to

baseline_text:
- **VAT payers (platitel) under § 4.** A taxable person with its seat, place of business or fixed establishment in Slovakia (or, failing that, its residence or usual abode there) becomes a payer from 1 January of the year after its turnover passed EUR 50,000, or at the supply that takes turnover in the current year past EUR 62,500 (VAT Act § 4(1)(a) and (b)). Voluntary registration is allowed (§ 4(6) and (7)). The registration tests sit in the sibling skill.
- **Foreign persons registered under § 5.** A business with no seat, place of business, establishment or residence in Slovakia becomes a payer from its first taxable supply in Slovakia, unless all its Slovak supplies fall in the § 5(2) list (for example supplies where the customer accounts for the tax, or supplies covered by OSS). It applies to the Bratislava Tax Office within five working days (§ 5(1) to (3)).
- **Persons who are not payers but owe tax under § 69.** Someone registered only under § 7 or § 7a, or not registered at all, who receives a reverse-charge supply files a return only for the month the liability arose, and does not pay if the tax is EUR 5 or less (§ 78(3)).
- **Out:** a business below the § 4 thresholds that is not a payer charges no VAT and files no periodic VAT return. It must still check § 7 and § 7a.

- **VAT payers (platitel) under § 4.** A taxable person with its seat, place of business or fixed establishment in Slovakia (or, failing that, its residence or usual abode there) becomes a payer from 1 January of the year after its turnover passed EUR 50,000, or at the supply that takes turnover in the current year past EUR 62,500 (VAT Act § 4(1)(a) and (b)). Voluntary registration is allowed (§ 4(6) and (7)). The registration tests sit in the sibling skill.
- **Foreign persons registered under § 5.** A business with no seat, place of business, establishment or residence in Slovakia becomes a payer from its first taxable supply in Slovakia, unless all its Slovak supplies fall in the § 5(2) list (for example supplies where the customer accounts for the tax, or supplies covered by OSS). It applies to the Bratislava Tax Office within five working days (§ 5(1) to (3)).
- **Persons who are not payers but owe tax under § 69.** Someone registered only under § 7 or § 7a, or not registered at all, who receives a reverse-charge supply files a return only for the month the liability arose, and does not pay if the tax is EUR 5 or less (§ 78(3)).

baseline_text:
- **Output tax.** Tax is charged on domestic supplies at the rate in force on the day the liability arises. The return also carries the tax the payer self-assesses as customer: intra-EU acquisitions of goods, services from foreign persons under § 69(3), and domestic reverse-charge supplies under § 69(12).
- **Domestic reverse charge (§ 69(12)).** Applies only when both supplier and customer are payers registered under § 4, § 4b, § 4c or § 5. It covers metal waste and scrap; greenhouse gas emission allowances; real estate the supplier has opted to tax under § 38(8); real estate sold in a forced sale; goods supplied when a security is enforced; cereals and oilseeds in chapters 10 and 12 not normally sold for final consumption; iron and steel in chapter 72 and headings 7301, 7308 and 7314; mobile phones and integrated circuits where the invoice tax base is EUR 5,000 or more; and construction work in section F of the classification, including goods supplied with installation in section F. The supplier invoices without VAT. The customer declares the tax and, if entitled, deducts it.
- **Input tax.** A payer deducts tax on purchases used for taxable supplies. There is no deduction for hospitality and entertainment (§ 49(7)(a)). Where purchases serve both taxable and exempt supplies, the deductible share follows the coefficient in § 50.
- **Passenger cars from 1 January 2026 (§ 85n).** For an M1 car, or an L1e or L3e motorcycle, acquired as a long-term asset, leased on a contract that is not short-term, or for goods and services bought to run one, from 1 January 2026 to 30 June 2028, the payer deducts 50%. Private use then counts as neither a supply of services nor a supply of goods. The cap does not apply to vehicles used only for car rental, paid passenger transport including taxis, driving schools, or as demonstration or courtesy cars (§ 85n(4)). It also does not apply where the vehicle is used only for business and the payer keeps electronic records for each vehicle: VIN, registration number, odometer readings at the start, at each period end and at the end, and a log of every trip with the driver, date and time, business purpose, start and end place and kilometres (§ 85n(5) and (6)). The payer must notify the tax office of a § 85n(4) or (5) use by the return deadline for the period of the first deduction. That notice is not needed for vehicles acquired by 31 December 2025 (§ 85n(9)).
- **Excess deduction (nadmerny odpocet).** If deductible tax is more than tax due, the excess is first set against the next period's liability. Any part not used is refunded within 30 days of filing the next period's return (§ 79(1)). A monthly payer registered at least 12 months, with arrears of not more than EUR 1,000 in the last 6 months, can mark the return and be refunded within 30 days of the return deadline for the period itself (§ 79(2) and (3)). The refund clock stops while a request to fix the return or control statement is open (§ 79(4)).
- **Rounding.** Figures in the return are rounded to the nearest euro cent, with 0.005 rounded up (§ 78(7)).

Exclude from **both N and D** a business/independent-business-part transfer, sales of assets used in the business other than inventory, occasional exempt financial services under § 39, and occasional property transfers/lettings. baseline_text: During the year use the previous year's coefficient. If it cannot be used, estimate a coefficient from the activity's nature **with the tax administrator's consent**. After year end calculate the coefficient from the completed year's actual values, recompute the annual deductible common-input VAT, and settle the difference from deductions already taken in the **last tax period of that year**, increasing or decreasing deduction as appropriate. Apply the same reconciliation for the part of a year during which a business became or ceased to be a payer. Where the accounting period is a financial year, that financial year replaces calendar year for these calculations ([§ 50(3)–(5)](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-50)).

baseline_text: **Domestic exemption catalogue.** In addition to insurance/financial services and the property rules, check the actual statutory exemption before treating a supply as exempt without input recovery: universal postal services and related goods under § 28; qualifying healthcare under § 29, which expressly does not exempt sales of medicines/medical aids; education meeting § 31's provider/legal conditions; and licensed lotteries/gambling under § 41. Apply § 49(3) to the associated inputs rather than importing the deduction rights of exports or intra-EU supplies ([§§ 28–41/49](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-28)).

baseline_text: **Transfer of a business.** A transfer or contribution of an enterprise, or a part forming an independent organisational unit, is outside the goods/services supply rules under § 10(1) if the acquirer is or becomes a payer under § 4(1)(d), subject to § 10(2)'s predominantly exempt acquirer exception and its exception for a predominantly exempt transferor. Do not enter it as an ordinary exempt sale without checking those conditions ([§ 10](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-10)).

baseline_text: **Private use and business gifts.** Subject to the specific § 85n vehicle treatment already described, withdrawal of goods for private use or free disposal can be a deemed taxable supply where input tax on the goods or their components was wholly or partly deducted. Business-purpose gifts with a value no greater than 17 euros excluding VAT per item, and business samples, are excluded from that deemed-goods-supply rule. Private use/free services have the separate § 9(2)–(3) rules. Business gifts are not a separate blanket deduction block in § 49(7): establish business use, apply the hospitality/entertainment block where it actually applies, and then check any deemed output tax ([§§ 8(3)/9](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-8), [§ 49](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-49)).

baseline_text: **Capital-goods register.** Separate resale inventory from long-term business assets. Under § 52a/54, the adjustment period includes the first-use year and is five calendar years for qualifying movable assets, and 20 calendar years for the listed property/building categories. The statutory investment-asset definition includes individually functioning movable items costing more than 1,700 euros excluding VAT, and the property categories in § 54(2)(b)–(c). Record original input VAT, initial deduction, first-use year and changes between taxable/exempt or business/private use. Apply § 54 for changed deduction entitlement and § 54a/54d for changed business/private use; perform the applicable adjustment in the final tax period of the year using Annex 1. For a non-calendar accounting year, § 52a(3) substitutes that accounting year. For assets whose adjustment period began by 31 December 2024, § 85kp(2) preserves the pre-2025 § 54/54a/54d and Annex 1 rules; check that transition before applying the current first-use method. The specific § 85n vehicle override still applies ([§ 52a](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-52a), [§§ 54–54d/85kp](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-54)).

baseline_text: **Credit notes.** Cancellation, returned goods and later price decreases/increases require the § 25 tax-base correction, subject to its specific exceptions. Under § 25(6), a post-liability price reduction to another payer can be left uncorrected for tax-base/tax purposes if both parties agree in writing; do not extend this exception to cancellations or price increases generally. A supplier reports the difference in the period the correction document is issued; a reverse-charge customer reports in the period it receives that document, subject to the statutory no-document rule. A customer that previously deducted input tax must reduce it when the base falls under § 53(1)(a); use the period of receipt or, if no document arrives within 30 days of the relevant event, the period in which those 30 days expire under § 53(2)(a). Correct the linked self-assessed output tax where the recipient was liable. Use the original transaction's rate under § 25(7), not a blanket reversal in the original return ([§ 25](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-25), [§ 53(1)–(2)](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-53)).

baseline_text: **Older office/property sale.** A sale of a building or qualifying part with its building land is exempt after the five-year test in § 38(1)/(7). That clock refers to first permitted/actual use, whichever is earlier, and can restart after the specified substantial works, including the 40% cost tests. An office sold six years after its relevant first-use event, without an intervening event restarting that clock, therefore meets the age condition. A payer can elect to tax an otherwise exempt qualifying non-residential sale under § 38(8); the election is barred for the listed residential categories. If the taxable sale falls under § 69(12)(c) between the prescribed registered payers, the buyer accounts for VAT. Do not invent a general buyer-consent condition absent from those provisions ([§ 38](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-38), [§ 69(12)(c)](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-69)).

baseline_text: **Vehicle boundaries.** N1 vans and N2+ trucks are outside § 85n's defined M1/L1e/L3e class. That removes the special 50% rule, but does not establish unrestricted deduction for private use or exempt activities: apply § 49's ordinary business-use and deduction conditions. For diesel 200 euros plus 46 euros VAT used wholly for taxable business in an N1 delivery van, 46 euros is deductible. The § 85n(1) acquisition cap concerns assets acquired from 1 January 2026; do not retrospectively halve an acquisition deduction merely because a pre-2026 car remains in use. Equally, pre-2026 acquisition did not itself guarantee 100% recovery. For mixed-use running goods/services bought during 1 January 2026–30 June 2028, § 85n(3) applies even when the car was acquired earlier; the notification exception for pre-2026 vehicles in § 85n(9) does not exempt those running costs from the substantive rule ([§ 49](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-49), [§ 85n(1)/(3)/(9)](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-85n)).

baseline_text: **Refund offsets and audited refunds.** Refunds remain subject to application against tax arrears under Tax Procedure Code § 79(1)/(7) and § 55(6)–(7); the old 10 euro minimum was not the statutory VAT rule. The Code's refund provision applies appropriately to excess VAT and uses a greater-than 5 euro cash-refund threshold under § 79(2)/(7). If an audit begins within the statutory refund window, VAT Act § 79(6) returns the amount established by the audit within 10 days after the audit ends, with the further final-decision/partial-protocol rules in § 79(6)–(7). There is no blanket 60-day audit or new-registration refund guarantee. A new payer that does not meet the 12-month fast-refund test follows the ordinary § 79(1) route already described. Statutory offsets count as a refund for these purposes ([VAT Act § 79](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-79); [Tax Procedure Code § 79(1)/(2)/(7)/(11)](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2009/563/20260901.html#paragraf-79)).

baseline_text: The control statement lists, invoice by invoice, every invoice issued for domestic taxable supplies or for domestic reverse-charge supplies under § 69(12)(f) to (j) (not simplified invoices) and every invoice received where the payer is the customer liable under § 69(2), (3), (6), (7) and (9) to (12), or deducts tax charged by another payer. Each line shows the counterparty's VAT number, invoice number, date of supply, tax base, tax, rate and deducted tax (§ 78a(2) and (4)). Simplified invoices received are given as totals, split by supplier once deducted VAT on them reaches EUR 3,000 in the period (§ 78a(6)). Retail sales are given as eKasa totals by rate (§ 78a(8)). A corrective statement replaces the original before the deadline; after the deadline, a supplementary statement carries only the changed lines (§ 78a(12)).

baseline_text: **Electronic return.** VAT payers deliver submissions electronically through the Financial Administration portal. Use the prescribed form valid for the period being corrected or filed; do not reuse the old Guide's unverified DPHv25 box table ([Tax Procedure Code § 14(1)(a)/15(4)](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2009/563/20260901.html#paragraf-14); [official portal's VAT-return guidance](https://www.financnasprava.sk/sk/podnikatelia/dane/dan-z-pridanej-hodnoty/danove-priznanie)).

baseline_text: **Adjacent goods reporting only.** A business with an INTRASTAT-SK reporting obligation files its monthly report electronically by the 15th calendar day after the reference month, including when its VAT period is quarterly. A weekend/public-holiday deadline moves to the next working day. This statistical report is separate from the VAT return; this restoration does not add an unverified 2026 reporting threshold ([Financial Administration INTRASTAT instructions](https://intrastat.financnasprava.sk/index.php?page=vsinfo), “Spôsob plnenia spravodajskej povinnosti”).

baseline_text: **Correcting the VAT return.** Before the filing deadline, a corrective return replaces the previous return. After the deadline, where tax should be higher or excess/refund lower, submit a supplementary return and pay the additional tax by the end of the month after discovery under § 16(2); § 16(3)(b) also requires correction of wrong VAT transaction data. A supplementary return can claim the permitted lower-tax/higher-refund correction under § 16(4), subject to § 16(7)–(9). Do not use a blanket four-year amendment window: the ordinary assessment period is five years from the end of the year the filing obligation arose, with the restart/maximum rules in § 69 and the special last-year extension in § 16(5). The audit restriction generally begins after 15 days from the specified audit notice/start event; the old statement that all amendment rights stop as soon as an audit starts was too broad ([Tax Procedure Code § 16](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2009/563/20260901.html#paragraf-16), [§ 69](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2009/563/20260901.html#paragraf-69); [January 2026 text](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2009/563/20260101.html#paragraf-16)).
