baseline_text: ## Cross-border points
closest_final_text: ## Cross-border points

baseline_text:
- **Services from abroad.** A Slovak business receiving a § 15(1) service from a foreign supplier accounts for the tax as customer (§ 69(3)). A non-payer receiving such a service from a supplier in another member state must first register under § 7a and then has no right to deduct; see the registration skill.
- **Intra-EU supplies of goods** are exempt under § 43 and go on the EC sales list. Exports are exempt under § 47. For goods exported under § 47(1)–(2), keep dispatch/transport evidence and the customs declaration confirming exit from the EU; § 47(3) supplies a specified alternative-evidence route for oral or deemed export declarations ([§ 47(3)](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-47)).
**Import self-assessment.** Normally customs assesses import VAT under § 84a(1), but the payer must self-assess in its VAT return under § 84a(3) when the conditions in § 84a(2) are met. For the ordinary route, the person on whose account the customs declaration is lodged must, when import liability arises, have a Slovak seat/business establishment or the stated residence, a § 4 or § 4b VAT number, and effective authorised-economic-operator status. The centralised-customs-clearance route instead permits the specified § 4/4b/5 payer with effective AEO authorisation. Obtain the customs declaration and authorisation; this is not a general election available to every VAT-registered importer. Declare qualifying import tax for its liability period and claim input VAT only to the extent § 49/51 permits. For an eligible fully taxable importer with a complete 23% import VAT base of 50,000 euros, output import VAT is 11,500 and deductible input VAT 11,500, giving zero net import VAT. The 50,000 must be the statutory import tax base, not customs value alone when duties/incidental costs must be added ([§ 84a](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-84a), [§§ 24/49/51](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/222/20260101.html#paragraf-24)). The § 68cb scheme for consignments of EUR 150 or less is a separate customs procedure for the person presenting the goods.
- **Foreign businesses** register under § 5 at the Bratislava Tax Office within five working days of becoming a payer. EU sellers to Slovak consumers can use OSS (§ 68a to 68c) instead.
- **EU SME scheme (from 1 January 2025).** A Slovak small business whose EU turnover stays at or under EUR 100,000 in the current and previous year can notify the Slovak tax office in advance and use small-business exemptions in other member states with an EX number (§ 68g). It files a quarterly report by the end of the following month. A business from another member state is exempt in Slovakia if its Slovak turnover stays at or under EUR 62,500 this year and EUR 50,000 last year and its EU turnover at or under EUR 100,000 (§ 68f). It loses the exemption from the supply that takes Slovak turnover past EUR 62,500 or EU turnover past EUR 100,000 (§ 68f(6)).
- **E-invoicing.** The version of the VAT Act in force from 1 January 2027 (Act 385/2025) changes invoicing and reporting. It is outside this 2026 skill.

baseline_text: **Example 1: a restaurant company, monthly return, March 2026.** Cafe Dunaj s.r.o. is a monthly payer. In March 2026 it sells EUR 40,000 net of goods and services at 23% (alcoholic drinks and takeaway sweets), EUR 10,000 net of restaurant meals at 5%, and EUR 2,000 net of non-alcoholic drinks served at the tables at 19%. Its domestic purchase invoices carry EUR 4,600 of deductible VAT. Output tax is 40,000 x 23% = 9,200, plus 10,000 x 5% = 500, plus 2,000 x 19% = 380, a total of 10,080. It deducts 4,600 and pays 5,480. The 25-day deadline ends on Saturday 25 April 2026, so the return, the control statement and the payment are due on Monday 27 April 2026 (Tax Procedure Code § 27(4)). Every invoice it issued (other than simplified invoices) and every full purchase invoice it deducts goes into the control statement line by line; simplified purchase invoices go in as totals and till sales as eKasa totals by rate.

It buys EUR 2,000 of advertising from an Irish company (a § 15(1) service), with no VAT on the invoice. In April it also buys an M1 passenger car for EUR 25,000 plus EUR 5,750 VAT. baseline_text: ## Ask the client first
closest_final_text: ## Ask the client first

baseline_text:
1. Which registration do you hold (§ 4, § 5, § 7 or § 7a), and since when? This decides whether you file every period and whether you can deduct at all. Obtain the exact VAT number and registration decision, including any group registration. The ordinary Slovak VAT-number format is SK followed by 10 digits; checking its format is not verification that the number is valid or that § 7/7a gives payer deduction rights ([official tax-authority country-format table](https://www.vero.fi/en/businesses-and-corporations/taxes-and-charges/vat/international-commerce/vat-number/vat-numbers-issued-by-different-eu-countries/)).
2. Are you on monthly or quarterly periods, and did turnover in any 12-month run reach EUR 100,000?
3. What do you sell, and at which rate? Food and restaurant clients need the 2026 split between 23%, 19% and 5%.
4. Did you buy, lease or run an M1 car or an L1e or L3e motorcycle in 2026, and do you keep the § 85n trip log?
5. Did you receive services from foreign suppliers, or buy construction work, scrap, steel, cereals, or phones and chips at EUR 5,000 or more from Slovak payers?
6. Do you make exempt supplies (financial, insurance, housing rental) as well as taxable ones?

baseline_text: Section 4 gives VAT-payer status (platiteľ), with output-tax and conditional input-deduction rights. Sections 7 and 7a give a VAT number for specified cross-border obligations without making the person a payer. A small business can owe recipient-accounted VAT before it reaches the domestic turnover threshold. The periodic return, detailed rate scopes, control statement and late-return penalties are in [slovakia-vat-return](slovakia-vat-return.md); income tax is in [slovakia-pit](slovakia-pit.md).

baseline_text: ## Who this applies to
closest_final_text: ## Who this applies to

baseline_text:
- Slovak sole traders (SZČO), s.r.o.s and other taxable persons with the domestic establishment or residence connection in §4(1), approaching the turnover threshold or considering voluntary registration.
- Freelancers and small agencies buying business services from EU platforms or supplying services to business customers in other member states. Section 7a has no monetary threshold.
- A taxable person not required to apply under §4 or §5, or a non-taxable legal person such as a sports club or foundation, acquiring goods from another member state: test §7 and §11.
- Businesses using older guidance must distinguish historical rules from current ones. The EUR 49,790 rolling-period threshold and 20% standard rate are historical, not the 2026 rules.

Section 4(1)(i) also has a separate rule for a person with only a Slovak fixed establishment, subject to its foreign-small-enterprise exception. This Guide covers §5 only where it interacts with the three registrations above.

closest_final_text: ## The taxable base

baseline_text: **The §4 turnover calculation.** Start with the value excluding VAT of goods and services supplied with their place of supply in Slovakia (§4(15)). Exclude supplies exempt under §28 to §36 and §40 to §42. Insurance (§37), property (§38) and financial services (§39) are generally included, but ancillary insurance and financial services supplied with another supply are excluded. Also exclude occasional disposals of tangible assets other than stock and occasional disposals of intangible assets. If the threshold is crossed exclusively through §37 to §39 exempt supplies, state that on the application (§4(3)); do not assume exemption eliminates registration.

baseline_text: Advance payments are not turnover until the supply occurs; supplies placed abroad and free supplies are outside the ordinary turnover count (FS method §1.5). The method's reverse-charge exclusion concerns supplies **received as buyer**, not a blanket exclusion for the business's own domestic sales. Purchases on which the business self-accounts are not its sales turnover. The supplier's own domestic supplies remain subject to §4(15). The property-specific advance-payment trigger in §4(1)(f), (g) must still be checked: an advance for a building, part of a building or building land can create payer status before delivery where the statutory condition is met.

baseline_text: **The two domestic turnover triggers.** Above EUR 50,000, payer status ordinarily starts on 1 January of the following year (§4(1)(a)); above EUR 62,500 it starts with the supply causing the excess (§4(1)(b)). That entire supply is taxed at its applicable rate, not merely the excess above the threshold (FS method §2.1). Legal succession, acquiring a payer's business or an independent business part, demergers and the other events in §4(1)(c) to (i) have their own status dates. Test those facts before applying the ordinary next-year rule.

baseline_text: **Historical transition.** Before 2025 the threshold was EUR 49,790 measured over up to twelve preceding consecutive calendar months. Section 85kn(1) preserves the former application/authority procedure for persons who reached that old threshold by 31 December 2024. The modern test uses a calendar year; historical 20% rates and seven-day §7/§7a decisions must not be applied to 2026 transactions.

baseline_text: **Voluntary §4 registration.** Before exceeding EUR 50,000, a person can apply under §4(6)(a), (7). It must be a taxable person carrying on economic activity. The authority's method recognises preparatory acts before the first sale, supported by evidence and the CJEU authorities C-110/94 INZO, C-268/83 Rompelman and C-527/11 Ablessio. Registration is effective on the date in the decision, with a 21-day decision limit; this ordinary voluntary route is not backdated before the application/decision (FS method §2.5). A fraud-based refusal requires objective evidence and an overall assessment, as explained in that method, rather than an unsupported assumption about the applicant.

baseline_text: After turnover has exceeded EUR 50,000 but before it exceeds EUR 62,500, §4(8) supplies two distinct early-status elections: mark the application to become a payer from the supply which exceeded EUR 50,000 (§4(8)(a)); or, **after the registration decision has been delivered**, notify an election taking effect the day after notification (§4(8)(b)). The first election is a separate statutory route and is not defeated by the ordinary voluntary no-backdating rule.

baseline_text: **Goods acquisitions under §7.** Apply before the acquisition taking the calendar-year net total to EUR 14,000 (§7(1)). The §11(4)(b) below-threshold exemption requires the threshold not to have been reached in the preceding year or the current year. New means of transport and excise goods are excluded from that count (§11(6)), but have their separate tax rules, so excluded from the count does not mean tax-free. Voluntary acquisition taxation below EUR 14,000 is allowed but binds the acquirer for at least two calendar years (§7(2), §11(7)). Section 7(4) avoids a duplicate application where the person is already registered under §7a or §4(7); it does not replace the acquisition-tax test.

baseline_text: For example, EUR 1,000 of taxable Meta Ireland advertising produces EUR 230 of Slovak reverse-charge VAT at 23%. A non-payer registrant cannot deduct it. A full payer using it wholly for deductible activity can self-assess EUR 230 and deduct EUR 230 under §49(2)(b), subject to §51. Voluntary registration affects both sale prices and input costs: if the business keeps a net price on a standard-rated sale, a consumer or exempt customer pays 23% more; if the gross contract price stays fixed, the supplier's net revenue falls instead.

baseline_text: ## Cross-border points
closest_final_text: ## Cross-border points

baseline_text: **Services under §7a have no monetary safe harbour.** A taxable person not required to apply under §4 must apply before receiving a service from a foreign person in another member state for which it owes tax under §69(3), or before supplying a §15(1) service placed in another member state for which the customer owes tax (§7a(1), (2)). A business spending only EUR 1 can still trigger registration. For EUR 30 of ordinary taxable EU advertising at 23%, the VAT is EUR 6.90: registration is still required before the service, and the liability month requires a return and payment under §78(3). A freelancer earning EUR 100,000 exclusively from ordinary §15(1) services to German business establishments can have zero domestic turnover and still require §7a registration.
